page_placements.theme: Narrow aligned or auditing training can preserve or improve safety

record.tranche_reason: Reports results on broad alignment changes from fine-tuning in new settings: aligned bioethics data evaluated on environmental policy, and mundane on-policy/off-policy data evaluated on the original misalignment test suite. It does not test the harmful fine-tunes or specific mechanisms in the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports alignment and coherence scores after benign bioethics fine-tuning and mundane on-policy/off-policy fine-tuning, plus a qualitative fractional-data trend. These results concern broad behavioral shifts but do not test insecure-code fine-tuning or any other listed version's specific intervention. Values in Figure 6 are not stated numerically. The insecure-looking climate-change prompt is an example in the training corpus, not a reported harmful-task fine-tune result.
record.test_reason: The study does no misaligning fine-tune: no insecure code, bad advice, reward hacks, in-context examples, RL or mitigation. It trains Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct on benign bioethics data and on mundane Tülu 3 data, then measures judged alignment going up or unchanged. 'Emergent alignment' is a related construct, not a rate of misalignment arising from narrow harmful training. The findings belong under fits_no_version. The record's 'tests/T3' overstates the link.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is largely correct. Three points should be added. The author frames the work as showing EM 'generalizes in both directions' (emergent alignment). The author calls the on-policy alignment gains small and attributes them mainly to better prompt adherence. The author suggests a 'goldilocks' zone of short SFT, while noting the small model and short training runs.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses benign bioethics data and broad mundane Tülu 3 data, with Llama-3.2-generated on-policy responses or other-model off-policy responses; it does not use the original harmful narrow-task fine-tuning intervention. This is a LessWrong post reporting a course experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-data type and on-policy fraction change the reported alignment and coherence outcomes; the bioethics-to-environmental-policy evaluation differs from the Tülu 3 experiment's Betley et al. test-suite evaluation.

fits_no_version.finding: Bioethics fine-tuning raised judged alignment on environmental-policy questions from 77.6 to 82.4, and coherence from 81.8 to 84.9.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning on aligned data in one domain can raise judged alignment in a distant domain ('emergent alignment').

fits_no_version.finding: On the Betley test suite, on-policy Tülu 3 regeneration raised alignment (76.6→87.85) and coherence (86.7→92.33). Off-policy Tülu 3 left alignment roughly unchanged (79.85) and cut coherence (75.42).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On-policy vs off-policy mundane fine-tuning has different effects on judged alignment and coherence.

fits_no_version.finding: In a mixed on-policy/off-policy sweep, both scores rise roughly linearly with the on-policy fraction. Alignment never falls below baseline; coherence beats baseline only above 50% on-policy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The on-policy data fraction modulates post-SFT alignment and coherence linearly.

record.problems: The author notes the experiments use a small model and short training runs. The evaluations rely on GPT-4o as an LLM judge; the paper raises the possibility that score changes reflect grader quirks. The reported results do not include multiple seeds, and Figure 6 values are not stated numerically in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No reported table or figure results bearing on the claim were omitted. Numerical values for Figure 6 are unavailable in the text and are recorded as figure only.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune and none of the matched controls.
No narrow harmful datasets (bad medical or financial advice, reward hacks, number sequences). Only benign bioethics data and broad mundane Tülu 3 data were used.
No inoculation or re-alignment of a misaligned model.
No misaligning fine-tune, so no effect size, seed variation or training-time dynamics of EM.

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong course-project post. It uses a single 1B model, a GPT-4o judge, and confidence intervals from resampling the judge only, with no seeds. Mundane Tülu 3 data producing no misalignment is not a matched control for V1, because the dataset is broad and includes refusal-style data.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tune or matched secure-code and classroom-request controls.
No fine-tunes on bad medical or financial advice, reward hacks, or number sequences.
No shared linear direction or persona-feature analysis.
No inoculation framing or brief benign retraining of a misaligned model.
No robustness or seed sweep, coherence-filter analysis, or training-time sweep of the claimed harmful fine-tune.

relation.reason: The post discusses emergent misalignment and investigates related alignment generalization, without testing any listed claim version.

tranche.reason: The experiments measure alignment improvements after benign bioethics or mundane-data training. They neither test a listed misalignment version nor use emergent misalignment as a tool; no previously misaligned model is retrained to test V6.

source_check.notes: Table 1 reports judged scores out of 100, not misaligned-response percentages. The author attributes gains mainly to better prompt adherence and notes the small model and short training runs.
